subject: Sorensen Health — unexplained p99 spikes and 5xx during on-prem UAT
messages:
From: Erin Sherman <erin.sherman@sorensenhealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: sorensen-oncall@sorensenhealth.com
Date: Tue, 13 Feb 2029 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes + 5xx during UAT — on-prem cluster

Olga,

We started UAT for phase 2 this morning and immediately saw a sustained p99 jump from ~420ms to 2.1s and a concurrent 5xx increase (mostly 502/503) for our on-prem VPC deployment. The window started 14:48 UTC and has been intermittent on and off since then — worst between 14:48–15:30 UTC.

Key observations from our side: 
- Errors concentrated on the decoder service: ~85% of 5xx come from the decode pods.
- The traffic pattern is identical to yesterday; no obvious spike in input QPS.
- Rolling restart of the decode pod reduces errors for ~8–12 minutes, then they return.

We attached RT logs and can share pod dumps if helpful. SLA for this environment is 99.9% availability for UAT; this is putting our regression window at risk.

Attachments: sorensen-rt-logs-20290213.tar.gz

Can you triage and confirm next steps? We need an ETA and any recommended mitigations (canary fallback to smaller model, route to hosted, etc.).

—Erin

Subject: RE: Sudden p99 spikes + 5xx during UAT — on-prem cluster

Olga / team — quick technical readout after initial log review.

Findings (first-pass):
- Decode pods show repeated decode-timeouts tied to a specific operator in the quantized decode kernel. Call stacks point to an AVX kernel falling back to a slower scalar path under certain tensor shapes; that fallback path exacerbates latency and triggers downstream health checks.
- Pod restarts temporarily flush the KV-prefetch cache, which explains the 8–12 minute temporary improvement.
- No clear increase in user QPS; this appears workload-shape sensitive (longer sequence tokens that trigger a different decode loop).

Immediate mitigations we can apply (proposed order):
1) Route a small fraction (5–10%) of traffic to the last-known-good float32 model variant (canary route) for 30–60 minutes to measure impact.
2) Adjust batch windowing to smaller batches for the decode service for the next 2 hours.
3) Ship a hotfix that pins kernel selection to omit the fallback codepath (requires controlled restart of decode pods; we estimate ~45–60m for rollout and verification).

Attachments: k8s-pod-dumps.zip

Request: Olga — do we have approval to flip the canary to float32 for Sorensen's UAT? If so, I will coordinate with orchestration to set traffic split and monitor.

Jonas Weber
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the rapid look, Jonas.

We applied the suggested small-batch flag locally per your guidance and saw p99 drop from ~2.1s to ~1.2s but 5xx persisted at ~1.5% of requests. We pushed a few test requests to the float32 canary on our side and saw success — p99 ~480ms.

I've attached a heap snapshot from one of the decode pods taken after a spike (heap-snapshot-20290213.txt). We can flip traffic to float32 on your side if that is the recommended next step; it looks promising.

Attachments: heap-snapshot-20290213.txt

—Erin

Subject: Exec summary & recommended customer-facing remediation (Sorensen)

Team — putting together a succinct exec note for Markus and the customer. Key points:
- Impact: Sorensen UAT experiencing elevated p99 (up to 2.1s) and transient 5xx (~1.5% during spikes).
- Root cause (probable): Decode kernel fallback triggered by shape/quantization interaction.
- Short-term remediation: Flip Sorensen UAT to float32 canary for 100% of UAT traffic for 1 hour, then observe (customer has validated float32 locally).
- Medium-term remediation: Push kernel selection hotfix + a conservative batch-size profile for Sorensen's workload.

Asks:
1) Approval to perform canary flip now and schedule hotfix rollout (Jonas to lead).
2) Approve a goodwill credit for SLA exposure (recommendation: one week of credits on UAT reserved capacity) — Erin has indicated regression-window SLA risk.
3) Prepare a short customer-facing incident note (Olga/Naomi) and a technical follow-up post-mortem (Jonas).

Related links: https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/SOR-2029-02-13, JIRA:INF-9281
